Fixed in hickory-proto 0.26.1. Istio ztunnel releases 1.28.x/1.29.x ship the hickory 0.25 stack until upstream tags a stable release migrating to hickory 0.26 (upstream main/release-1.30 use hickory 0.26 / hickory-net); locally replacing the Hickory resolver stack inside this image would materially diverge from Istio-source behavior.

Same NSEC3 closest-encloser proof validation infinite loop as RUSTSEC-2026-0118. ztunnel builds without enabling hickory-proto dnssec backends (dnssec-ring / dnssec-aws-lc-rs). The buggy NSEC3 walk inside DnssecDnsHandle is exercised only once an application wraps resolvers with DNSSEC verification; Istio ambient DNS forwarding in src/dns proxies lookups and echoes EDNS DO without running DnssecDnsHandle-backed validation paths.

Same provenance as GHSA-82j2-j2ch-gfr8: rustls-webpki 0.102.8 is reached only through the optional `boring-rustls-provider` git dependency, gated behind the `tls-boring` Cargo feature, which the ztunnel build never enables (default features for runtime, `tls-openssl` for FIPS). The crate is listed in Cargo.lock but is not compiled into the binary.

rustls-webpki 0.102.8 enters the Istio 1.28 Cargo.lock only via the optional `boring-rustls-provider` git dependency, which is gated behind the `tls-boring` Cargo feature (`tls-boring = ["dep:boring", "dep:boring-sys", "boring-rustls-provider/fips-only"]`). The image is built with default features for the runtime variant and `--no-default-features --features tls-openssl` for the FIPS variant; neither path enables `tls-boring`, so `boring-rustls-provider` and its bundled rustls-webpki 0.102.8 are not compiled into the ztunnel binary. The vulnerable code is present in the lockfile-derived SBOM but absent from the produced artifact. Istio 1.29 removes this dependency entirely.

GHSA-cq8v-f236-94qc requires crates.io rand to be compiled with its optional `log` feature plus additional runtime conditions (recursive logging touching ThreadRng while it reseeds). textnonce declares `rand = "0.7"`, which resolves to rand 0.7.3 with default features (`std`), and `cargo tree -p rand@0.7.3 -e features` confirms the optional `log` feature is inactive, so the unsound specialization is absent from the built crate graph.

False positive. CVE-2026-22184 affects the untgz utility that is part of zlib source code, but Debian zlib packages (zlib1g and zlib1g-dev) do not ship the untgz utility by default. For Debian Trixie (and other versions), zlib comes from zlib1g (binaries) and does not include the untgz binary. The vulnerability scanner incorrectly flags zlib packages as vulnerable when the untgz utility is not actually present in the installed packages.
